goldens.comment: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

goldens.comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
goldens.reasoning: C2 identifies the same issue: a missing sender key in integration.metadata causes a KeyError.

candidates: OAuthLoginView uses pipeline.signature as the OAuth state value which is deterministic (md5 of pipeline view FQNs) rather than a per-session random nonce, weakening CSRF protection and allowing state replay across sessions

GitHubInstallation assumes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] exists; if metadata.sender is missing or malformed (legacy data, partial state, or manual DB changes), this will raise KeyError/TypeError and 500 the flow instead of showing the failure dialog

OAuthLoginView does not reliably handle exceptions from the GitHub /user call (which raises on non-2xx) and does not catch failures around the token exchange request, leading to 500s instead of the intended failure UI

The OAuth authorize redirect URL is built via string interpolation rather than urlencode, which can create invalid URLs if values contain reserved characters and omits standard OAuth params like response_type=code

GitHubInstallation queries Integration.objects.get(external_id=...) without filtering by provider, but Integrations are only unique on (provider, external_id), which can raise MultipleObjectsReturned or pick the wrong integration if IDs collide across providers
